title: CPSC, Distributors Announce Recall of "FIRE CAP" Fire and Smoke Suppressants
summary: The product does not suppress fires and could intensify fires. Units: More than 136,000.

title: Pull Toys Recalled by Manhattan Group LLC
summary: The wooden wheels and pegs attached to the toy could come off, presenting a choking hazard to young children. Units: About 3,400.

title: Race Car Collectibles Recalled by Action Performance Companies
summary: The fluorescent light base of the unit becomes extremely hot and can melt, presenting a fire hazard. Units: About 1,600.

title: CPSC, Prometheus International Inc. Announce Recall of Novelty Lighters
summary: The lighters do not have any child-resistant mechanisms, as required by the Consumer Product Safety Act. Young children could ignite the lighters, presenting a fire hazard. Units: About 4,000.

title: Toy Chests Recalled by Thornwood Furniture
summary: The lids on these toy chests could fall onto a child's head or neck. An investigator for the Georgia Office of Consumer Affairs discovered the problem with the toy chest while conducting retail surveillance for CPSC. Units: About 400.

title: CPSC, Shopko Stores Inc. Announce Recall of Baby Garments
summary: The rose-shaped buttons on these garments can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: Approximately 9,800.

title: Ladies' Robes Recalled by HANRO USA
summary: The robes fail to meet federal flammability standards for clothing and can ignite readily, presenting a serious risk of burn injuries. Fabrics that do not comply with the standard typically burn faster than newspaper. Units: About 2,100.

title: Men's Sweatshirts Recalled by Eddie Bauer
summary: The sweatshirts, which fail to meet federal mandatory standards for fabric flammability, could ignite readily and present a serious risk of burn injuries, in violation of the Federal Flammable Fabrics Act. Fabrics that do not comply with the standard typically burn faster than newspaper. Units: Abou

title: Vanguard Engines and Fuel Filters Recalled by Briggs & Stratton
summary: The fuel filters on these engines can leak gasoline, posing a fire hazard to consumers. Units: About 2,600.

title: CPSC, Cadet Recall In-Wall Heaters; Settle Lawsuit
summary: Flames, sparks or molten particles can spew through the front grill cover of the heater into the living area of a residence, putting consumers at risk from fires, including burn injuries, smoke inhalation and property damage. title: CPSC, Mountain High Hosiery Ltd. Announce Recall of Tommy Hilfiger Socks for Infants and Children
summary: The heat-sealed Tommy Hilfiger flag logo appliques on these socks can detach, posing a choking hazard to young children. Units: Approximately 360,000.

title: CPSC, TSI Prime Inc. Announce Recall of Ceiling Light Fixtures
summary: The light fixtures can short circuit, posing a fire hazard. Units: About 126,000.

title: CPSC, Nordstrom Inc. Announce Recall of Infant and Toddler Jackets
summary: Snaps located on the flap pockets of these jackets could be removed, presenting a choking hazard to infants and young children. Units: Approximately 2,250.

title: CPSC, New Cole Sewell Corp. Announce Recall of Storm Doors
summary: These storm doors were manufactured without retaining pins in the upper windows. The upper window can fall out and could injure nearby consumers. Units: About 23,000.

title: CPSC, Dynacraft Industries Inc. Announce Recall of Mountain Bikes
summary: The front suspension forks on these bikes might not have been welded properly, and can break apart during use, resulting in serious injury to the rider. Units: About 19,000.

title: CPSC, Frieder Inc. Announce Recall of Power Strips
summary: The wiring in these power strips is undersized and poses shock, electrocution and fire hazards. Units: About 35,000.
